On Tue, 4 Aug at 7:20 AM , Cory Shepherd <coryshepherd1@hotmail.com> wrote:
CAUTION: This email originated from outside of our organisation. Do not click links or open attachments unless you
recognise the sender and know the content is safe.
Good morning,
| am seeking an indicative proposal — scope, approach and fee range — for an independent
psychosocial risk assessment of a 24/7 hospital switchboard room in the Brisbane region: a small team
of operators on a rotating roster across day, evening, night and weekend shifts, handling a high daily
call volume including emergency codes and distressed callers.
The assessment contemplated would be conducted under the Managing the risk of psychosocial
hazards at work Code of Practice 2022 (Qld) and consistently with ISO 45003, and would include:
review of recorded data (call demand, rosters, leave, incident and complaint records); the People at
Work survey; on-site observation across shift types, including night and weekend shifts; interviews
offered to all operators; risk rating with a controls report; and a twelve-month review point.
For transparency: | am an employee of the workplace concerned, preparing a contribution to a
consultation process about how such an assessment might be conducted. Any engagement would be
commissioned by the employer, not by me. At this stage | am asking only:
whether this is within your service scope;
your indicative approach;
an indicative fee range for an assessment of this size;
your current availability; and
one scope question — whether the assessment's deliverables could include a statement of the role's
psychosocial demands and working conditions in a form suitable for use by treating medical
practitioners when providing fitness-for-work, restriction and adjustment opinions for workers in the
room.

I'm happy to take this by email or a short call.

Kind regards,

Cory Shepherd
